newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares tumble, index off 2.23 pct at start.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares tumble, index off 2.23 pct at start.

text.p: ** (0445 GMT) - Bombay blue chips take a beating in early
deals, benchmark index falls 96.29 pts, or 2.23 pct, to
** Bombay bourse opens after four-day holiday; dealers
expect lacklustre trade amid absence of fund buying
** Monday's fall of over two percent at National Stock
Exchange pushes prices down at the Bombay bourse
** Market's short-term trend weak but dealers say they do
not expect sharp downside from current levels
Share prices took a sharp hit in early deals at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday when trade resumed after a four-day holiday, dealers said.
A weak trend at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Monday where the index fell over two percent triggered the correction at the Bombay bourse, they said.
Among individual stocks, Asian Paints rose 11.0 rupees, or 3.3 percent, to 341.0 at the Bombay bourse after ICI Plc on Monday said it had purchased a 9.1 percent stake in the firm.

The British chemicals and paints group said in London it had agreed to purchase 3.67 million shares at a price of 351.0 rupees per share. Bombay-based finance firm Kotak Mahindra Capital Company said it had purchased the shares from the Choksey family, one of four original promoters of Asian Paints.
"Thereafter, Kotak Mahindra Capital Company has agreed to sell these shares to ICI Plc at 351 rupees per share subject to approval," ICI said in a statement.
